title: HTML and JavaScript Integration
description: Learning how to embed JavaScript in HTML and interact with the DOM using event attributes.

flashcards.question: How do you include JavaScript code directly inside an HTML file?
flashcards.answer: By using the `<script>` tag inside the `<head>` or `<body>` sections.

flashcards.question: What is the purpose of the `onclick` attribute in HTML?
flashcards.answer: It defines a JavaScript function to be executed when an element is clicked.

flashcards.question: Name two other common event attributes besides `onclick`.
Where is the recommended place to include the `<script>` tag for better page loading?
flashcards.answer: At the end of the `<body>` section, before the closing `</body>` tag.

flashcards.question: How can you link an external JavaScript file in HTML?
What does DOM stand for and why is it important in JavaScript?
flashcards.answer: Document Object Model; it represents the page so JavaScript can manipulate content and structure.

flashcards.question: How do you access an element by its ID in JavaScript?
What is the difference between inline JavaScript and external JavaScript?
flashcards.answer: Inline JavaScript is written directly inside HTML elements or `<script>` tags, while external JavaScript is in separate `.js` files.

flashcards.question: What is event bubbling in the context of JavaScript events?
flashcards.answer: It is the process where an event propagates from the innermost element up through its ancestors.

flashcards.question: Why is it important to separate HTML and JavaScript in larger projects?
flashcards.answer: For better maintainability, readability, and reusability of code.
